text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 10 in history.
1444 - Turks under Amurath II defeated Janos Hunyadi and his army of Hungarians and Poles at the battle of Varna.
1483 - Martin Luther, German religious reformer who began the Protestant Reformation, born.
1493 - Paracelsus born as Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim; He was an alchemist and physician who played a leading role in establishing the role of chemistry in medicine.
1668 - Francois Couperin, French composer known as "Le Grand" who was a central figure in French harpsichord music, born.
1683 - George II, king of England 1727-1760 and the last British monarch to take part in a battle (Dettingen, 1743), born.
1697 - William Hogarth, British painter and engraver famous for his pictorial satire, born.
1728 - Oliver Goldsmith, author of "She Stoops to Conquer" and "Vicar of Wakefield", born in Ireland.

1759 - German dramatist and poet Johann Christoph Friedrich von Schiller born; author of "Don Carlos" and "Die Rauber" as well as the poem "An die Freude" (Ode to Joy) which Beethoven used for his Ninth Symphony.
1889 - British actor Claude Rains, who starred in the films "Casablanca", "Robin Hood" and "Caesar and Cleopatra", born.
1919 - Mikhail Kalashnikov, Russian engineer and designer of the AK-47 rifle that bears his name, born.
1925 - Welsh stage and screen actor Richard Burton, twice married to and divorced from Elizabeth Taylor, born.
1928 - The Regent Hirohito was crowned Emperor of Japan. He had effectively become head of state and named Regent when his father became ill in 1920 and he ruled until his death in 1989.
1938 - Mustapha Kemal Ataturk, the first president of Turkey from 1923 and founder of the modern secular state, died.
1982 - Soviet statesman Leonid Brezhnev died; he had been leader of the Soviet Union from 1964 and state president from 1977.
1989 - Bulgarian leader Todor Zhikov stepped down as Communist Party chief and head of state after 35 years in power.
1990 - Veteran socialist leader Chandra Shekhar was sworn in as India's new prime minister at the head of its second minority government in less than a year.

1995 - President Alija Izetbegovic of Bosnia and Franjo Tudjman of Croatia initialled an agreement shoring up their federation in the first breakthrough of U.S.-led talks aimed at ending four years of war in the former Yugoslavia.
